---
order: 3
unit: track
title: A water tracker
summary: "Build a water tracker with a goal: add a glass, reset the day, and see a message and a progress bar. An Every tick event keeps the display in step without setting the text in every button's event. A condition that isn't a trigger, such as comparing a variable, is checked every tick, and an action only waits for a sub-event's condition if it sits inside that sub-event."
language: maths
shape: build
hook: "Most apps show the same numbers in several places. Keeping them all up to date by hand in every button gets messy fast; there's a simpler way."
pacing: { keyDelayMs: 40, cursorMs: 500, afterActionMs: 300, postRollMs: 1200 }
voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 }
app:
  command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-appbuilder" 8753
  url: http://127.0.0.1:8753/index.html
  readySelector: "[data-ab='tab:design']"
  layout: full
explainClip:
  query: { code: "@app.json#done", tab: run, id: explain }
  caption: "Every tick keeps the screen in step"
  say: "Every tick keeps the screen in step with the variables."
  clip:
    - caption: { text: "The Add button's event only adds 1. Every tick sets the text.", say: "The Add button's event only adds one. Every tick sets the text." }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - caption: { text: "The cap is inside the sub-event, so it stops at the goal.", say: "The cap is inside the sub-event, so it stops at the goal." }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - click: { selector: ".view-run [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
    - expect: { selector: ".view-run .stage", contains: "Glasses: 8 of 8" }
    - caption: { text: "Goal reached: the message and the bar follow the variable too.", say: "Goal reached. The message and the bar follow the variable too." }
    - wait: 1600
---
In the practice tracker, the Save event changed the total *and* set the text. That works with one button, but with three or four buttons you'd need a Set text in every one, and it's easy to miss one.

This time you'll use **Every tick**. App Builder checks the events over and over, about 60 times a second. An Every tick event runs on each of those checks, so it can keep the screen in step with the variables, whatever changed them.

![The water tracker: "Glasses: 5 of 8", a progress bar five-eighths full, Add a glass and Reset buttons, and the message "Keep going".](app.svg)

## Try the finished app

```step
stage: info
insight: "Using the finished tracker, with its events beside it, gives a target for the build and shows Every tick running all the time."
try: { playground: appbuilder, starter: "app.json#done", tab: run, level: 2, height: 600 }
check: { type: reflect, text: "I added glasses until I reached the goal and tried to go past it. It stopped at 8, and the Every tick row kept lighting up." }
```

This is the finished app you'll build, open on the **Run** tab. Under it, the Every tick row keeps flashing: it runs all the time, not just when you click.

## Build 1: the display, every tick

```step
stage: run
app: true
query: { code: "@app.json#start", level: 2, id: build-1 }
caption: "Every tick keeps the text right"
clip:
  - caption: { text: "Two variables first: Glasses starts at 0.", say: "Two variables first. Glasses starts at zero." }
  - type: { selector: "[data-ab='new-variable-name']", text: "Glasses" }
  - press: Enter
  - caption: { text: "Goal starts at 8: type the name, then the starting value.", say: "Goal starts at eight. Type the name, then the starting value." }
  - type: { selector: "[data-ab='new-variable-name']", text: "Goal" }
  - type: { selector: "[data-ab='new-variable-value']", text: "8" }
  - press: Enter
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='tab:events']" }
  - caption: { text: "A new event. Its condition is in System: Every tick.", say: "A new event. Its condition is in System. Every tick." }
  - click: { selector: ".view-events [data-ab='add-event']" }
  - click: { selector: ".view-events .ev.sel [data-ab='add-condition']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='group:System']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='entry:everyTick']" }
  - caption: { text: "Its action sets GlassText from both variables.", say: "Its action sets GlassText from both variables." }
  - click: { selector: ".view-events .ev.sel [data-ab='add-action']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='group:object:GlassText']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='entry:setText']" }
  - type: { selector: "dialog[open] [data-ab='param:value']", text: "\"Glasses: \" & Glasses & \" of \" & Goal" }
  - click: { selector: "dialog[open] [data-ab='done']" }
  - expect: { selector: ".view-events .preview-col .stage", contains: "Glasses: 0 of 8" }
  - caption: { text: "The preview already shows it: Every tick set the text.", say: "The preview already shows it. Every tick set the text." }
  - wait: 900
insight: "An Every tick event keeps the display in step with the variables on its own, whatever changes them."
try: { playground: appbuilder, starter: "app.json#start", keep: build, level: 2, height: 640 }
check:
  type: code
  text: "Variables Glasses (0) and Goal (8), and an Every tick event that sets GlassText from them."
  rules: { contains: ["variable Glasses = 0", "variable Goal = 8"], event: [["when Every tick", "Set GlassText text to", "Glasses", "Goal"]] }
```

The screen is made for you: GlassText, AddButton and ResetButton.

1. Under **Variables** on the left, add *Glasses* starting at 0, and *Goal* starting at 8.
2. On the **Events** tab, choose **+ Add event**, **+ Condition**, **System**, **Every tick**.
3. Add the action **GlassText**, **Set GlassText text to …**: `"Glasses: " & Glasses & " of " & Goal`

## Build 2: the Add button, with a cap

```step
stage: run
app: true
query: { code: "@app.json#sol-step-2", level: 2, id: build-2 }
caption: "The button only changes Glasses"
clip:
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='tab:events']" }
  - caption: { text: "AddButton adds 1 to Glasses. No Set text needed.", say: "AddButton adds one to Glasses. No Set text needed." }
  - click: { selector: ".view-events [data-ab='add-event']" }
  - click: { selector: ".view-events .ev.sel [data-ab='add-condition']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='group:object:AddButton']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='entry:onClicked']" }
  - click: { selector: "dialog[open] [data-ab='done']" }
  - click: { selector: ".view-events .ev.sel [data-ab='add-action']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='group:Variables']" }
  - click: { selector: "[data-ab='entry:addTo']" }
  - type: { selector: "dialog[open] [data-ab='param:value']", text: "1" }
  - click: { selector: "dialog[open] [data-ab='done']" }
  - wait: 600
  - click: { selector: ".view-events .preview-col [data-ab='widget:AddButton']" }
  - expect: { selector: ".view-events .preview-col [data-ab='widget:GlassText']", contains: "Glasses: 1 of 8" }
  - caption: { text: "Every tick showed the new count.", say: "Every tick showed the new count." }
  - wait: 800
insight: "The build includes the cap exactly as many beginners write it, so the next steps can test it and find why it doesn't stop at the goal."
try: { playground: appbuilder, starter: "app.json#sol-step-2", keep: build, level: 2, height: 640 }
check:
  type: code
  text: "AddButton is clicked adds 1 to Glasses, with a sub-event that checks Glasses < Goal (built as set out, slip and all)."
  rules: { event: [["when AddButton is clicked", "Add 1 to variable Glasses"], ["when AddButton is clicked > when Variable Glasses < Goal"]] }
```

1. Add an event: **AddButton**, **AddButton is clicked**. Add the action **Variables**, **Add … to variable**: 1 to Glasses. Click Add in the preview: the count changes, because Every tick sets the text.
2. Now a cap, so it stops at the goal. Click the AddButton event, then its **⋯** button, and choose **Add a sub-event**. Give the sub-event the condition **Variables**, **Variable … … …**: Glasses **<** Goal. Leave the Add 1 action where it is, on the AddButton event.

## Build 3: Reset, then test

```step
stage: run
insight: "Testing past the goal shows the cap doesn't hold, which the Check step explains."
try: { playground: appbuilder, starter: "app.json#sol-step-3", keep: build, level: 2, height: 640 }
check:
  type: code
  text: "ResetButton is clicked sets Glasses to 0."
  rules: { event: [["when ResetButton is clicked", "Set variable Glasses to 0"]] }
```

1. Add an event: **ResetButton is clicked**, with the action **Set variable … to …**: Glasses to 0.
2. In the preview, click Add 12 times. What does the screen say? Then click Reset.

## Check: did the cap work?

```step
stage: investigate
insight: "Tracing the cap and reading the goal message test the two halves of the move: what a sub-event's condition controls, and conditions checked every tick."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "You built the cap as in Build 2 and clicked Add 12 times, with a goal of 8. What did the screen say?"
      options: ["Glasses: 12 of 8", "Glasses: 8 of 8", "Glasses: 7 of 8", "Glasses: 0 of 8"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Try it again, and count. Did it stop at 8?", "The cap didn't hold it back at all.", "Reset sets it to 0, but only when you click Reset."]
      explain: "It went past the goal. The Add 1 action sits on the AddButton event, so it runs on every click. The sub-event's condition only controls actions inside the sub-event, and there are none."
  - check:
      type: bug
      code: "working.txt#cap"
      text: "This is the cap you built. Click the line that lets the count pass the goal."
      answer: 2
      fault: logic
      misconception: action-outside-subevent
      explain: "Line 2: the action is on the parent event, so it runs on every click. The sub-event's condition below it only controls actions inside the sub-event. Move Add 1 into the sub-event."
```

### What did you see?

### Find the slip

## Build 4: fix the cap

```step
stage: run
insight: "Moving the action into the sub-event is the fix, and testing at the goal confirms students now know which actions a condition controls."
try: { playground: appbuilder, starter: "app.json#built", keep: build, level: 2, height: 640 }
check:
  type: code
  text: "Add 1 to Glasses is inside the sub-event, and no longer on the AddButton event itself."
  rules: { event: [["when AddButton is clicked > when Variable Glasses < Goal", "Add 1 to variable Glasses"]], lacks: ["event: when AddButton is clicked | do: Add 1 to variable Glasses"] }
```

Move **Add 1** into the sub-event: click the action on the AddButton event and choose **Delete**, then click the sub-event, choose **+ Action** and add it there. Then click Add 12 times in the preview again.

| When (condition) | Do (actions) |
|---|---|
| ⚡ AddButton is clicked | |
| ↳ Variable Glasses < Goal | Add 1 to variable Glasses |

## Make it yours: a message and a progress bar

```step
stage: modify
insight: "The message and progress bar use the every-tick idea twice, plus an Else from last lesson, so the move is used in a new place."
try: { playground: appbuilder, starter: "app.json#sol-step-6", keep: build, level: 2, height: 640 }
tasks:
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "The bar is a box 300 pixels wide when full. Glasses is 2 and Goal is 8. What width should the bar be?"
      options: ["75", "150", "37.5", "100"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "That would be half full, 4 of 8.", "That's 300 ÷ 8, one glass's worth.", "There's no glass amount that gives 100 here."]
      explain: "2 of 8 is a quarter, and a quarter of 300 is 75. In App Builder: Glasses / Goal * 300."
  - check:
      type: code
      text: "A Message that says \"Goal reached!\" or \"Keep going\" (an event with Else), and a bar, BarFill, whose width follows Glasses every tick."
      rules: { event: [["when Variable Glasses = Goal", "Set Message text to"], ["else", "Set Message text to"], ["when Every tick", "Set BarFill width to", "Glasses", "Goal"]] }
```

### Work out the width

### Build it

- **Message:** add a Text and rename it *Message*. Add an event **Variables**, **Variable … … …**: Glasses **=** Goal, with the action **Set Message text to** *Goal reached!*. From the event's **⋯** menu, choose **Add an Else below**, and give the Else the action that sets it to *Keep going*.
- **Progress bar:** add a **Box** and rename it *BarBack*: grey, 300 wide. Then add another Box, *BarFill*, in blue, the same size and in the same place (set X and Y in Properties). The one added later sits on top. In the Every tick event add **BarFill**, **Set BarFill width to …**: `Glasses / Goal * 300`

```teacher
summary: Students build a water tracker with two variables (Glasses, Goal), an
  Every tick event that keeps the display up to date, Add and Reset buttons, and
  a cap. The cap is first built the way beginners often write it (Add 1 left on
  the AddButton event, the check in a sub-event), so it fails at the goal;
  students find why and move the action into the sub-event. The Make step adds a
  goal message with Else and a progress bar.
time: 60
timing: Try 5 min · Build 1–3 20 min · Check 8 min · Build 4 5 min · Make it
  yours 20 min
goals:
  - I can use Every tick to keep what's on screen up to date.
  - I can say which actions a sub-event's condition controls.
  - I can make a progress bar from a number.
struggle: The deliberate slip in Build 2 can feel like a trick. Say up front
  that the build includes one mistake beginners often make, and the class will
  find it together.
before: >
  The cap in Build 2 is wrong on purpose: Add 1 stays on the parent AddButton
  event, so it runs on every click and the sub-event's condition (Glasses <
  Goal) controls nothing. The Investigate step finds it; the Modify step fixes
  it by deleting the action and adding it again inside the sub-event (App
  Builder has no drag between events; the ⋯ menu and + Action do it).


  Every tick runs about 60 times a second. Setting text there is fine. Adding to
  a variable there is not (it would add 60 a second), which is why the exit
  question asks about it.


  The Build step's tick boxes accept the slip on purpose (they check the cap as
  built); Build 4's tick only comes once Add 1 is inside the sub-event.


  Pick any goal and thing to track if water doesn't suit your class (pages read,
  laps, minutes outside). The app is about counting towards a goal, not health
  advice.
running:
  - "Before Build 2 (whole class, on the deck): the Add event only adds 1, with
    no Set text. Does the count change? Compare with lesson 1."
  - "Build 3: everyone clicks 12 times before anyone explains."
  - "Check: draw the event and its sub-event on the board; circle which actions
    belong to which."
  - "Make it yours: work out one bar width together before students build it."
stuck:
  - see: The count shows the word Glasses or the & signs.
    ask: Which parts are inside the quote marks?
    fix: Only the words to show go in quotes; the variables and & go outside.
  - see: The bar doesn't move.
    ask: Which event sets its width, and is it on BarFill?
    fix: The Set BarFill width action goes in the Every tick event.
  - see: After the fix, Add does nothing.
    ask: Where is the Add 1 action now?
    fix: It should be inside the sub-event, beside Glasses < Goal, not deleted.
stretch: Let the user set their own goal with a text input and a Set goal button
  (int() from lesson 1).
support: Give the finished Every tick event as a table and have students check
  theirs row by row.
leads: "Next: Values journal, with three screens, a choice that carries between
  them, and a list."
exit:
  q: What goes wrong if you put "add 1 to Glasses" in the Every tick event?
  a: It adds 1 about 60 times a second, so the count shoots up. Every tick is for
    keeping the display in step, not for changing the count.
explain: >
  **Every tick** runs about 60 times a second, so an Every tick event that sets
  the text keeps the screen in step with the variables, whatever changed them.


  A condition without a ⚡, such as **Variable Glasses = Goal**, is checked every
  tick too, and stays true while the comparison holds.


  A **sub-event's** condition only controls the actions inside the sub-event. An
  action on the event above it runs whenever that event runs.
solutions:
  step-7#t2: app.json#sol-make
class:
  inquiry:
    q: "A screen shows the same number in three places: a count, a bar and a
      message. How could you make sure all three always agree?"
    prompts:
      - What if a new button changes the number? What would you have to remember?
      - Is there a way to update them without remembering?
    notes: Setting the display in every event is easy to forget. An Every tick event
      keeps everything in step with the variables, whatever changed them.
  activities:
    - at: investigate
      kind: discussion
      title: Which actions does the condition control?
      minutes: 5
      do: >
        Draw the AddButton event with its sub-event as two boxes, one inside the
        other. Ask students to place the Add 1 action where step 7 put it. Ask:
        when the condition Glasses < Goal is false, which box is skipped? Is the
        action in it?
      notes: A sub-event's condition only controls what's inside the sub-event.
```
